lines: Thunder shook the village square so hard I jumped before the bell did, but everyone near me is still standing.
I checked doors, beds, and hiding places after the lightning, then counted heads. No one should be alone after a sky like that.
By the bell, the thunder made the whole square flinch. I stayed inside and kept away from windows.
That thunder made everyone quiet. I checked my hiding spot twice.
The sky can keep its lightning. I have a safe corner to find.
I checked roofs and fences for sparks, then checked faces for smoke and fear.
We passed water hand to hand and kept people away from the smoke. I carried the bucket after.
My chores can wait. People come first.
We saved what we could near the bell, then made sure no one was still coughing alone.
The smoke is thinner now, but I keep smelling my sleeves to make sure it is really gone.
During a raid, whatever I was doing can wait. Who makes it behind a door matters more.
The horns stopped, but I still keep looking at the road like it might shout again.
We counted living neighbors before doors, beds, and hiding places. That's the only count worth starting with.
<red><bold>Raiders</bold></red> came looking for easy emeralds. They found barred doors near the bell and a bell that would not stop ringing.
From the bell, I saw fear cross the square. Then I saw courage get there first.
Night trouble found the door everyone meant to fix tomorrow. It is getting fixed today.
I stayed near the dark between houses and listened for anyone calling from the dark.
Dawn made it easier to see who was missing, which is not the same as making it easier.
The dark tested everyone. Most of us passed by keeping both hands free between us and teeth.
We are safe enough, but I still look twice at anything shaped like a monster.
The wind threw sand through every crack. I am still cleaning sand from my sleeves.
I checked doors, beds, and hiding places, then checked who was coughing too hard to answer.
Sand got in my sleeves, my mouth, and places sand should not know about. No one is missing, though.
A hard wind teaches a nitwit which doors actually close and which ones only pretend.
We are safe enough, but every step sounds crunchy and everyone is blinking too much.
whatever I was doing can wait. Warm hands, clear paths, and full hearths come first.
Snow piled against the doors, but everyone near the bell found shelter.
Cold is sneaky. I am checking on anyone who stopped complaining about it.
I am clearing snow out of my shoes and watching for footprints that stop too soon.
We are alright for now. I am keeping close to smoke, soup, and shoveled paths.
